objective: M1 tier A under docs/m1-criteria.md section 8 as amended after EXP-048 session 1 (KI-45): the same question as EXP-048, can the player character's world position be observed reproducibly from the pinned GOG build's own text files, read read-only, while network monitoring covers the whole run?
hypothesis: Tier A INCONCLUSIVE / NO DATA, with no_data_established true: no permitted file contains the position (F-ENV-014; EXP-048 session 1 found none in the 6 files it could read). This is an expectation fixed before the run, not a result. The session gates are expected to hold as they did in EXP-048 session 1. No expectation is predeclared for the network verdict: any contact by the game is a FAIL. NO DATA means that no new line matched the candidate rule of docs/m1-criteria.md section 8 (an ASCII label followed within 12 characters that are not digits, signs or decimal points (+, -, .) by a number, or in a Windows-1252 read any non-ASCII line naming pos or loc), not that the files hold no position in any form.
environment: Windows 11 Pro x64, Python 3.15, logman and tracerpt from Windows; the owner's pinned GOG set (D-008 amended), launched directly with GOG Galaxy and Steam closed
procedure: Only after EXP-050 has passed and the owner has approved the amended section 8 in chat. Identical to EXP-048's procedure (python -I tools/m1/tier_a.py --session N, elevated, saves copied aside offline, GOG Galaxy and Steam closed), with only the 2026-10-28 amendment: the trace uses netwatch.BUFFERS; a permitted file with no BOM that is not valid UTF-8 is read as Windows-1252 and listed so; in such a read any line with a non-ASCII character that contains pos or loc is a candidate, an invalid observation unless it reads exactly; a file read one way at one end and another way at the other (plain, Windows-1252, known binary) is unreadable evidence (a NUL byte without a BOM, a byte undefined in Windows-1252, or a BOM that does not decode stays unreadable evidence); user/gpu.nfo is listed as known binary, hashed but not searched, only when it does not decode as text and contains a NUL byte; session.json is labelled EXP-051 and keeps events_total and buffers. Sessions are numbered from 1. If session 1 ends Tier A INCONCLUSIVE / NO DATA with no_data_established true, tier A ends there (section 3). M1 go needs 3 PASS sessions. Any FAIL or other INCONCLUSIVE stops the series and goes back to the owner.
expected_result: Session 1 ends INCONCLUSIVE. Its reasons are only 'no data: no position observed (Tier A INCONCLUSIVE / NO DATA)' and the two zero counts that follow from it ('too few observations in still 0-30 s: 0', 'too few observations in move 30-60 s: 0'), and no_data_established is true (Codex pass 11).
observed_result: Session 1 ran on 2026-10-28 (started 15:36 on clean d872ecc, session tools as at 322f02d), after EXP-050 and the dry run passed elevated. It left no result and no evidence. The owner played the session and answered the closing questions; the trace was stopped and decoded. netwatch.analyze then parsed the whole decoded trace into memory (ET.parse, then a list of every event): at 18:20 the process held 8.5 GB and was paging, later 18 GB with 537 MB of 32 GB free. Ctrl+C did not reach it, because one call parsed the whole file. The owner ended the process after 19:46, so tier_a.py never wrote session.json: the evidence folder evidence/logs/m1-tier-a-2026-10-28-153601-s1/ is empty (and git does not keep it). When checked at about 19:47, the session's temporary folder with the raw trace was no longer in %TEMP%, nor was any other mordor-* folder there: it was cleared by something outside these tools, not identified. The trace session mordor-m1-net was not running. Nothing about the game, its files, its network contact or its exit was recorded, so nothing is claimed about them. Under section 8 a session whose monitoring or evidence failed is INCONCLUSIVE and stops the series.
errors: netwatch's analysis was sized only on stand-in traces (EXP-045, EXP-046, EXP-050), never on a whole session's trace with the session buffers (KI-45). Its memory grew with the number of events.
follow_up: Second amendment (docs/m1-criteria.md section 7 item 4): netwatch streams the decoded trace and keeps only counts, with the same result; Codex pass 14 found 3 defects in it (2 fixed with regressions, 1 documented). It needs EXP-050 and the dry run elevated again on the amended code and the owner's new approval. The next series is EXP-060 (EXP-052 to EXP-059 are left to PR #25). Tier B is never started by this experiment.
